across each of the surfaces separately.\n\n- First, we consider the upper cone $S_1.$ \n\nWe compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y){:}$\n\n$$\n\\begin{aligned}\\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\\frac{∂}{∂x}(2-\\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}})=-\\frac{x}{\\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\\\ \\frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\\frac{∂}{∂y}(2-\\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}})=-\\frac{y}{\\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\\end{aligned}\n$$\n\nIf we denote $\\mathbf{F}=\\langle P, \\, Q, \\, R \\rangle,$ then\n\n$$\nP = x, \\qquad\nQ = 0, ={∬}_{D}(-P\\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\\text{d}A \\\\  & ={∬}_{D}-x\\cdot (-\\frac{x}{\\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}})-0\\cdot (-\\frac{y}{\\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}})+(-{y}^{2})\\,\\text{d}A \\\\  & ={∬}_{D}\\frac{{x}^{2}}{\\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}-{y}^{2}\\,\\text{d}A,\\end{aligned}\n$$\n\nwhere $D$ is the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane.\n\n- Next, we consider the lower plane $S_2.$ \\text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\\cdot n\\,\\text{d}S \\\\  & ={∬}_{D}⟨x,0,-{y}^{2}⟩\\cdot ⟨0,0,-1⟩\\,\\text{d}A \\\\  & ={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\\,\\text{d}A.\\end{aligned}\n$$\n\nTherefore, the flux of
